scope.summary: Build the pose editor UI hooks per Section 13.27 GUI clauses: draggable IK pin handles (hands/feet/knees) driving the MT-519 full-body IK, a pose library browser applying BodyPose assets with morph-context re-solve, and the multi-actor alignment display for couple/group sex poses placed as one asset (AREQ-002/003/017 surfaces).
acceptance_criteria: IK pin handles render in the viewport on hands/feet/knees; dragging a handle drives the full-body IK solver live and the pin state (pinned/free, target transform) is saved into the pose asset.

The pose library browser lists BodyPose assets with thumbnails and tags (incl. the porn-range QA pose set); applying a pose re-solves for the current body's proportions (a petite and an obese body both keep feet grounded on the same asset).
Multi-actor pose assets display relative root alignment between 2+ bodies with stage-anchor indicators; applying places all actors in one operation.
Pose symmetry mirror and pose blending controls are exposed (MT-522 surface).
All handles and controls carry stable author_ids; Argus drives pin-drag -> capture headlessly.

MT-718 exclusively owns PoseKit/character-sheet source selection, binding, evidence verification, lift derivation, reprojection, and proposal-diff UI; this MT owns committed or amended 3D BodyPose editing, pose-library use, IK handles, and multi-actor placement using the same typed command/state model.

Manual joint corrections from MT-718 open this editor as an immutable amended proposal; accept/reject/remap decisions and revert remain visible in History and never create a parallel UI-only pose state.

The exact TailorSurfaceDescriptor row MT-631 enumerates every route, pane, control author_id, dynamic entity-key rule, action, state, help anchor, permission, undo policy, receipt, and command binding; wildcard-only evidence is rejected.

Applicable blank, loading, populated, stale/conflict, cancelled, failed, retry, permission, keyboard/focus, narrow/4K/DPI, overlap/clipping, and no-focus-steal states are covered by the registry-derived Argus matrix.
scope.risk_if_missed: Posing stays keyboard-and-API-only, making scene work (the daily production activity) slower than Daz's weak-but-usable Active Pose — a regression against the tool being replaced.

surfaces: Tailor BodyKit committed/amended 3D pose editor and pose library

target_entries: Tailor UserManual > BodyKit workspace and controls

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: This MT owns authoritative, job, or external-tool lifecycle events and must project the same event_id, run_id, actor_id, and correlation_id from EventLedger into Flight Recorder.
This MT must wire the shared internal_diagnostics API for its native, job, device, solver-run, or DCC failure modes with bounded structured evidence.
Long-running, native, or external-process work must register bounded progress and child/process identity with the shared Palmistry watcher; Tailor must not fork a watcher.

risks: Broad MT scope can hide multiple review targets.
Markdown MT lists may disagree with packet-declared active/next MT truth.
Receipt routing may target an old MT if contract identity is omitted.
minimum_controls: Exactly one primary proof target per MT unless the packet records why not.
MT identity must be stable and referenced by receipt correlation.
Generated projection drift must not wake Coder or Validator by itself.

required_changes_before_execution: Add PoseKit deep-link/import, sidecar preview, 2D-to-3D reprojection, ambiguity/confidence/joint-map/contact/conflict/stale-version panels and concrete Argus coverage.
BodyKit GUI must expose or integrate the geometry/morph, joint, weight/rigidity, transfer, skin/material, interlink, Jobs, Problems, history, recovery, and shared-world contracts.
Consume the signed technical refinement, canonical command/surface registries, classified HBR tiers, and task-oriented UserManual contract before execution.
